about.text: I am a Senior Researcher in XR Standards at LG Electronics, building NEXA ONE to turn product design files into 3D Gaussian Splatting training data using exact camera poses and 3D points instead of structure-from-motion. With method and parameters unchanged, its point clouds raised average PSNR from 37.74 to 39.27 dB with NVIDIA NuRec (3DGUT) and from 34.63 to 38.00 dB with Postshot on 5 appliance datasets.

My work also spans synthetic ground-truth labels and simulation / 3D VQA systems, target-less CLOiD camera calibration that cut projection error from over 20 px to under 5 px, and MCP / LangGraph LLM agents whose "optimize for web" test reduced a 207.54 MB asset to 4.80 MB in one iteration.
I received my M.S. and B.E. in Electronics Engineering from Sogang University. My graduate research covered camera pose estimation and multi-view stereo for omnidirectional imaging.

bullets.text: Built NEXA ONE, a 3ds Max plugin that turns product design scenes into 3D Gaussian Splatting training datasets using exact camera poses and 3D points instead of structure-from-motion. On 5 appliance datasets, NEXA point clouds raised average PSNR from 37.74 to 39.27 dB with NVIDIA NuRec (3DGUT) and from 34.63 to 38.00 dB with Postshot, with method and parameters unchanged.

Calibrated the uncalibrated head RGB cameras of LG's CLOiD humanoid robot without a calibration target: SAM2 arm segmentation, forward-kinematics pose initialization, and optimization of 5 distortion and 6 pose parameters against the robot's 3D model cut projection error from over 20 px to under 5 px.

Added pixel-aligned ground-truth labels to a synthetic 3D data pipeline: metric depth and surface normals as unfiltered 32-bit float EXR, automatic object-ID masks with an annotation file, and dataset-wide depth bounds computed from 8 bounding-box corners per camera instead of every vertex.

Stood up Scenesmith agentic indoor-scene generation, SplatTalk 3D VQA and vLLM serving of Qwen3.6-35B across 2 L40S GPUs on a SLURM cluster; loaded Gaussian Splat scenes into NVIDIA Isaac Sim 6.0 and documented its splat rendering artifacts.

Prototyped a LangGraph pipeline for robot-learning simulation-scene context: household purchase records feed member personas, a simulated family discussion, appliance placement and long-horizon robot task queries; run on made-up sample data.

Researched importance-weighted camera placement for Gaussian Splatting using image gradients, depth edges, SAM3 segmentation and OCR lifted into a 3D importance field; built a 23-scene appliance dataset and labeling tool. In a preliminary result on one scene, naive close-ups lowered important-region PSNR to 33.78 dB versus 35.02 dB orbit-only; a patch-crop training schedule recovered 34.98 dB and reached 35.25 dB.
Developed an MCP-based tool that lets marketers run 3D asset optimization autonomously, then extended it into a self-improving LangGraph agent with agentic optimization loops.

Implemented a LangGraph agent in which an LLM selects a preset, then a capped measure / decide / optimize loop gives it measured metrics (gltf-transform) and targets; it accepts the result or sets the next RapidCompact parameters. On a test asset, "optimize for web" took 207.54 MB to 4.80 MB (-97.7%) and 2,607,777 to 231,456 triangles (-91.1%) in one iteration.

Built an MCP server exposing V-Ray-to-PBR conversion and optimization to an LLM chat through a sequential job queue with progress tracking and e-mail notices; reworked the pipeline into headless Blender background jobs to fix context errors in server threads.

Automated the optimization of high-fidelity 3D assets (3ds Max + V-Ray) for web and mobile AR: 200+ assets, average file size from about 4 GB to about 4 MB, deployed on LG.com (US) so customers can view TV products at real scale.

Built 3DGTP AUTO, a Python tool for headless 3ds Max preprocessing, V-Ray-to-PBR conversion, preset-driven mesh and texture optimization with combinatorial parameter sweeps, and Blender post-processing to GLB and USDZ. Wrote a screen-image replacement script with automatic inspection renders and used it to update 136 TV assets, each checked in iPhone AR.

Built an interactive display demo with 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructed from V-Ray renders, integrating HTC Vive tracking with Unreal Engine 5 nDisplay for real-time parallax; rendered in real time at 4K and presented to executive leadership. The V-Ray baseline takes about 40 minutes per frame on average.
Fixed an ELoom3D cloth-simulator bug that made single-UV garments load slower than multi-UV ones; after the fix, a sample garment loaded in 0.06 s (single UV) vs. 0.21 s (multi UV).
Improved automatic quad-mesh post-processing of Instant Meshes output for simulated garments: removed flipped and overlapping faces and merged nearby vertices without opening holes.

publications.title: MosaicMVS: Mosaic-Based Omnidirectional Multi-View Stereo for Indoor Scenes
publications.abstract: We present MosaicMVS, a novel learning-based depth estimation framework for a mosaic-based omnidirectional multi-view stereo (MVS) camera setup. It uses a regular field of view (FOV) MVS network for an omnidirectional imaging setup with explicit consideration of hypothetical voxel-wise FOV overlaps. The resulting depth predictions are accurate and agree on the omnidirectional multi-view geometry. Unlike existing MVS setups, MosaicMVS camera setup can be easily applied to omnidirectional indoor scenes without having to account for constraints such as intricate epipolar constraints and the distortion of omnidirectional cameras. We validate the effectiveness of our framework on a new challenging indoor dataset in terms of depth estimation, reconstruction, and view synthesis. We also present new evaluation metric to check reconstruction performance using post-processed masks for accurate evaluation without any ground truth depth map or laser-scanned reconstructions. Experimental results show that our framework outperforms the state-of-the-art MVS methods in a large margin in all test scenes.
publications.summary: Learning-based multi-view stereo depth estimation for a mosaic-based omnidirectional camera setup in indoor scenes, with a new indoor dataset and a mask-based reconstruction metric. Joint first author.

publications.title: Camera pose estimation framework for array-structured images
publications.abstract: Despite the significant progress in camera pose estimation and structure-from-motion reconstruction from unstructured images, methods that exploit a priori information on camera arrangements have been overlooked. Conventional state-of-the-art methods do not exploit the geometric structure to recover accurate camera poses from a set of patch images in an array for mosaic-based imaging that creates a wide field-of-view image by sewing together a collection of regular images. We propose a camera pose estimation framework that exploits the array-structured image settings in each incremental reconstruction step. It consists of the two-way registration, the 3D point outlier elimination and the bundle adjustment with a constraint term for consistent rotation vectors to reduce reprojection errors during optimization. We demonstrate that by using individual images' connected structures at different camera pose estimation steps, we can estimate camera poses more accurately from all structured mosaic-based image sets, including omnidirectional scenes.
publications.summary: A camera pose estimation framework that exploits the known array structure of mosaic-based image sets (two-way registration, 3D point outlier elimination, rotation-constrained bundle adjustment), including omnidirectional scenes. Joint first author.

figures.caption: FIGURE 2 Example of generalized omnidirectional camera rig. (A) Top cross-section view of the mosaic-based omnidirectional camera rig. (B) Side cross-section view of the mosaic-based omnidirectional camera rig
figures.alt: Two line drawings of a ring-shaped multi-camera rig. (A) Top view: cameras sit around a circle, lines from the centre mark an equal angular step between neighbours, and overlapping blue view cones show adjacent fields of view. (B) Side view: cameras lie on a vertical arc with the same overlapping cones.

figures.caption: FIGURE 3 Overall flowchart of the proposed framework

Steps: undistortion; correspondence search; two-way registration (vertical and horizontal image registration and essential matrix estimation, 3D point triangulation); 3D outlier elimination; fusion; bundle adjustment. Outputs: camera poses and point cloud.

publications.title: Structured Camera Pose Estimation for Mosaic-Based Omnidirectional Imaging
publications.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
publications.abstract: This paper presents a novel structured camera pose estimation framework for mosaic-based omnidirectional imaging, i.e., producing a wide field of view (FoV) image that covers an entire sphere of the surroundings from a set of regular FoV images. With the effective utilization of geometric priors, the proposed framework exploits an individual image's connected structure while sequentially extracting correspondence between them. In the proposed framework, 2DSfM, a structure from motion method for multi-view images in structured 2D grids, is also proposed. Additionally, we propose a constraint term for rotation vectors in the bundle adjustment process that efficiently incorporates structural priors. We demonstrate our framework on structured omnidirectional image scenes and compare to existing frameworks. The experimental results show that our framework outperforms well-known conventional frameworks regarding both average reprojection error and reconstruction results.
publications.summary: Structured camera pose estimation for mosaic-based omnidirectional imaging: 2DSfM, a structure-from-motion method for images in structured 2D grids, plus a rotation-vector constraint in bundle adjustment. Joint first author.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overall flow of the proposed framework.
figures.alt: Block diagram, left to right: input images with internal camera parameters; correspondence search (feature extraction, feature matching, outlier elimination); 2DSfM (initialization, 2D image registration, triangulation), loop closure and bundle adjustment with a re-triangulation loop; output camera poses and 3D structure.

publications.title: Understanding the Limitations of SfM-Based Camera Calibration on Multi-View Stereo Reconstruction
publications.abstract: The recent success on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) research has triggered the interest to improve the stereo reconstruction. There have been many considerations to reconstruct unstructured general images. However, photos taken in an unstructured environment are not well applied to previous research techniques. This paper proposes a robust method in this special environment. First, camera parameters are extracted using two types of Structure-from-Motion (SfM). In general, intrinsic camera parameters are extracted via camera calibration, and extrinsic parameters are computed by SfM. After that, we put these parameters as an input into two types of multiview stereo methods and compare the results of each methods. Finally, the structured indoor dataset which is called ETRI 360° dataset has better reconstruction results compared with unstructured dataset by using specific SfM and MVS methods.
publications.summary: Compares two Structure-from-Motion camera calibrations as input to two multi-view stereo methods, and shows better reconstructions on the structured ETRI 360° indoor dataset than on unstructured data. Second author.

publications.title: Apparatus for estimating camera pose using multi-view image of 2D array structure and method using same
publications.abstract: Disclosed herein are an apparatus for estimating a camera pose using multi-view images of a 2D array structure and a method using the same. The method performed by the apparatus includes acquiring multi-view images from a 2D array camera system, forming a 2D image link structure corresponding to the multi-view images in consideration of the geometric structure of the camera system, estimating an initial camera pose based on an adjacent image extracted from the 2D image link structure and a pair of corresponding feature points, and estimating a final camera pose by reconstructing a 3D structure based on the initial camera pose and performing correction so as to minimize a reprojection error of the reconstructed 3D structure.
publications.summary: Granted US patent on estimating camera poses from multi-view images of a 2D array camera system through a 2D image link structure and reprojection-error correction; extends the ISCAS 2021 work.

projects.title: NEXA — 3D Design Files to Gaussian Splatting Training Data
projects.summary: NEXA ONE turns product design scenes into 3D Gaussian Splatting training datasets, exporting exact camera poses and 3D points instead of structure-from-motion. Structure-from-motion fails on repetitive and textureless surfaces; it failed on a massage-chair scene, while NEXA removes that estimation step.

bullets.text: Showed NEXA point clouds are a drop-in input upgrade: on 5 appliance datasets with method and parameters unchanged, average PSNR rose from 37.74 to 39.27 dB with NVIDIA NuRec (3DGUT) and from 34.63 to 38.00 dB with Postshot.

Built the 3ds Max plugin with automatic camera trajectories, exact camera poses and renderer-derived intrinsics exported in COLMAP format, point-cloud initialization, live camera previews and a non-blocking batch render loop for V-Ray CPU/GPU and scanline.

Designed view-proportional, occlusion-aware point sampling with a custom 3ds Max ray caster: per-object voxel grids, bounding-sphere pre-culling and backface culling place colored points only on surfaces the cameras actually see.

Implemented shape-adaptive camera placement: ray-cast probing builds a pseudo-hull around an arbitrary scene and a Fibonacci lattice spreads cameras uniformly over it, so the user sets only the camera count.

Wrote the Python preprocessing CLI (Open3D, OpenCV, NumPy) to merge rendered camera sets, back-project depth into colored point clouds with voxel averaging and statistical outlier removal, extract masks, and convert datasets for Postshot, nerfstudio and research trainers.

projects.title: Importance-Weighted Camera Placement for Gaussian Splatting
projects.summary: Research on importance-weighted camera placement, lifting image gradients, depth edges, SAM3 segmentation and OCR into a 3D importance field for camera selection. Results are preliminary; the close-up training experiment covers one scene.

bullets.text: Researched per-view importance heatmaps lifted into a 3D importance field for Gaussian Splatting camera selection; built a 23-scene appliance dataset and a labeling tool.

Measured that uniformly adding views saturates: tripling a Gaussian Splatting capture from 300 to 900 uniformly placed images changed PSNR by at most +0.14 dB, motivating importance-aware camera placement.

Built a single benchmark harness for next-best-view / active view selection, running FisherRF, MUSIQ, ACP, CrossScore and a random baseline from their released code, plus re-implementations of SA-RegGS and my own method.

Preliminary result on one scene: naively adding close-up images lowered PSNR on the semantically important region to 33.78 dB versus 35.02 dB orbit-only; a patch-crop training schedule recovered 34.98 dB and reached 35.25 dB.
